column1: # cutover-rows.tsv -- every row bin/cutover-check.sh grades, as data.
# WHY DATA: a row used to be three lines of bash plus its prose, so twenty-five
# of them priced more than the prose ratchet allows and the check could not grow
# to the size that would make it trustworthy. Same shape as unarmed.tsv.
# id  section  token  expect  label  why
# expect:  absent   the token must not appear (residue, and things that must stay gone)
#          present  it must appear at least once
#          all      it must appear once per account -- MUST-KEEP, so a partial is a FAIL
# The probe in cutover-check.sh emits the tokens; that half is code because it
# runs on the far host. This file decides what each one MEANS.
# THREE SECTIONS, and the last two are the ones that rot. "The new thing works"
# is easy to satisfy while the old thing sits beside it still armed -- so B
# checks for what should no longer EXIST, and C asserts what must SURVIVE.
# C is what makes the report safe to ACT on: a cleanup driven by B alone can cut
# something load-bearing and still read green. Every C row is graded per account
# (`all`), so losing one path on one account is a FAIL, not a rounding error.
# SCOPE EVERY ROW TO THE HOST BEING GRADED. B5 names conf files by basename
# because `_paced.monkey.conf` on vaporwave is monkey's live config: "cleaning
# that up so vaporwave passes" would break the host that still dispatches.
# A ROW IS CHEAP ON PURPOSE. The first version of this check had ten rows
# written as bash, Zach did not trust it, and it could not grow because each row
# also cost prose against the ratchet. Rows here are data and cost nothing, so
# the honest answer to "what else would prove it" is always: add the row.

column6: every tick asks github.com whether it may run a local job

column6: absent, every tick HOLDs at rc=127 and reads as a busy quota

column5: the host has a host-mode dispatch clock
column6: no PACED_HOST_MODE row in root's crontab means nothing dispatches

column5: the build carries lib/gh-app-token.sh
column6: without it the runner cannot mint, falls back to root's ambient auth, and holds MILESTONE-BLIND on every row -- silently, before LIB-MISSING existed

column5: host mode resolves BOTH App credentials from /etc/selfdev
column6: the conf alone mints nothing; SELFDEV_GH_APP_SH was the half that was missing

column5: the host-wide Claude token is readable by root
column6: root has no ~/.claude/.credentials.json, so without this every dispatch dies at the model call

column5: the host state dir records a real DISPATCH
column6: WOULD-DISPATCH and MILESTONE-BLIND are not dispatch; a runner that has never dispatched is stalled, not idle

column5: no verdict state under /root
column6: root drives but the job runs AS the account; a verdict here means reader and writer disagree about whose home it is

column5: no nightly-batch state under /root
column6: same split-brain, the other half

column5: usage-gate's LEGACY_SCHED_DIR is unreachable
column6: a conf dir under a person's home is a second source of schedule truth

column5: no account carries a scheduler clone
column6: the whole point of gen-2; each is a second, staler copy of the dispatcher

column5: no per-account RUNNER crontab row
column6: host mode dispatches for all of them; these double-dispatch

column5: ONE build pin per host (#180), no per-account verb-builds
column6: $HOME/.local/bin precedes /usr/local/bin, so their verbs resolve into a staler build

column5: no account-mode rotation state left behind
column6: a second rotation pointer for a rotation that no longer exists

column5: no conf in the build names a per-account clone path
column6: on a clone-free host every one of those rows is a path that cannot exist

column5: no ~/.selfdev-setup/ left from provisioning
column6: scaffolding that outlived the build it scaffolded

column5: no per-account ~/.local/libexec/selfdev/
column6: #887: one copy of the host tools per account, each free to go stale on its own

column5: no per-account release-tick status file
column6: the account-private clock's own state, for a clock that should be the host's

column5: no second selfdev-release:TICK row per account
column6: the host-wide tick already runs; these race it

column5: no per-account App credential under ~/.config/selfdev
column6: one host-wide key (#624); per-account copies drift and cannot be rotated together

column5: no per-account ~/.local/bin/usage-gate.sh
column6: dose-project.sh prefers it over the build's, so a stale copy silently outranks the shipped one

column5: no nightly-batch working clone per account
column6: another clone by another name

column5: no url.*.insteadof rewrite in any account's git config (#171)
column6: a rewrite makes every remote lie about where it points

column5: no ~/handrun.log
column6: the residue of a human running the loop by hand

column5: every account keeps ~/.claude/settings.json
column6: without it the account has no permissions, no hooks, and dispatches into a refusal

column5: every account keeps ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml
column6: the fallback auth every gh read lands on when no App token is minted

column5: every account keeps ~/.local/share/scheduler-registry
column6: the registry IS the account's memory of what it has run

column5: every account keeps its own scheduler-verdict dir
column6: this is where the job writes; deleting it is how the split-brain becomes permanent

column5: every account keeps ~/tmp
column6: the .profile TMPDIR block points here; without it every job writes to a shared /tmp

column5: every account is still in group selfdev
column6: the group is what reads /etc/selfdev; losing it is losing every credential at once

column5: every account still has linger enabled
column6: without linger the account's units die at logout and the host dispatches into nothing
